problem: Embodied RL agents rely on reward shaping, imitation, mapping modules or extra sensors. Generic self-supervised auxiliary losses (CPC, inverse dynamics) give no guarantee of encoding task-relevant semantics, and task-specific supervised auxiliary losses don't transfer across tasks.
motivation: Simulators expose rich ground-truth metadata (object poses, rooms, relations) that is available only at training time. Using it as a general-purpose training-only supervisory signal could yield semantic, history-aware belief states without needing that metadata at inference. Explicitly decoding a variable-size scene graph is expensive in an RL loop, so a cheaper alignment mechanism is needed.
key_idea: Iteratively build a ground-truth scene graph of what the agent has seen, encode it with a GNN, and use a contrastive (InfoNCE-style) loss to align the agent's recurrent belief at step t with the graph embedding of step t, as an auxiliary loss to DD-PPO.
insight: Contrastive alignment with a graph encoder is enough to inject semantic, spatial and memory information into the belief, with no graph decoder. The ablations show that retaining history matters (SGC without history is worse than RL: SR 34.8 vs 41.0 on RoboTHOR, with 60.6% false End actions). Object positions matter (about 4 points of SR). A well-chosen rich signal beats a task-specific one: an RL+Visibility loss falls below RL (54.8 vs 62.4 SR), while SGC beats RL+CPCA-16 by about 4.6 SR. Linear probes and fast adaptation to novel goal categories confirm the belief encodes more semantics and free-space information.
method: Iterative scene graph: Nodes are the agent, the current room and every object seen within a distance threshold (each instance is its own node). Nodes persist after leaving view, so the graph keeps the episode history. Node features are an object-type embedding plus 3D position relative to the agent, refreshed every step.

Edge relationships: Directed edges encode 13 relations recomputed each step from simulator poses and geometry: Sees, Holds, Touches, On, Near, Adjacent, Right, Left, Above, Below, Front, Behind, Contains (room/object/agent).
Graph encoder: Three Graph Attention layers followed by a global max-pool give a graph embedding g_t per step.

Contrastive SGC loss: MLP_b(b_t) and MLP_g(g_t) project the GRU belief and the graph embedding. A dot-product matrix P is built over the batch of steps, softmax and cross-entropy use the diagonal (t=s) as ground truth. Graphs from neighbouring steps of the same episode act as automatic hard negatives.
Efficient training: The graph is computed at only about 20% of randomly sampled timesteps. The SGC loss is added to the DD-PPO loss, and the graph, encoder and MLPs are used only in training.
Agent architecture: Frozen CLIP-ResNet50 visual encoder, GRU belief and linear actor-critic (EmbodiedCLIP-style), trained in ProcTHOR-10k houses via AllenAct.

setting.backbone: Frozen CLIP-ResNet50 + GRU + actor-critic, trained with DD-PPO (+ SGC auxiliary loss with a GAT graph encoder)
setting.training_data: ProcTHOR-10k training houses via RL only: 350M steps for ObjectNav, 180M for MultiON, 90M for ArmPointNav (7,000 houses). No demonstrations. Scene-graph supervision comes from simulator metadata.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB only (plus target object type embedding; relative goal coordinates for ArmPointNav)
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level: MoveAhead, RotateLeft/Right (30°), LookUp/Down, End (ObjectNav); Found for MultiON; arm move actions for ArmPointNav
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR (evaluated on ProcTHOR-Val, RoboTHOR, AI2-iTHOR, ArchitecTHOR, ManipulaTHOR)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth scene metadata (object poses, rooms, relations) used only at training time for the SGC loss; none at test time

numbers_note: The main results table (Table 1: ProcTHOR-Val, RoboTHOR, AI2-iTHOR, ArchitecTHOR ObjectNav, MultiON-2/3, ArmPointNav) is missing from the provided text. Only the gains quoted in the prose are available, and these are not used as own-method numbers: ObjectNav SR +12% on ProcTHOR-Val, +12% RoboTHOR, +9% AI2-iTHOR, +5% ArchitecTHOR; MultiON-2 SR +2.3% and SPL +5.5%; MultiON-3 SR +8% and SPL +4%; ArmPointNav SR +3.3% and SRwD +2.4%. The ProcTHOR-Val numbers from the ablation table (70.8 vs 62.4 SR) give a gain of 8.4, which differs from the +12% quoted in the text for Table 1.
results: SGC as an auxiliary loss to DD-PPO improves ObjectNav in-domain and zero-shot across four benchmarks, with SR gains of roughly 5-12 points (e.g. RoboTHOR SR 53.4 vs 41.0 for RL). It also improves MultiON-2/3 and ArmPointNav. On ProcTHOR-Val it beats RL+CPCA-16 (66.2 SR), RL+Visibility (54.8) and RL (62.4). SGC agents produce far fewer false End actions (14.9% vs 45% on RoboTHOR), adapt faster to novel goal categories, and have better linear-probe accuracy for visibility, memory and free-space.
limitations: Building iterative scene graphs and computing relations adds training-time overhead (e.g. MultiON training takes 5 days vs 2 days for RL alone), so graphs are computed at only about 20% of steps.

Requires privileged simulator metadata at training time and uses a vanilla GAT encoder; only RL baselines and two other auxiliary losses are compared, with no comparison to other SOTA navigation pipelines.
